historical_territory: Các thực hành ghi nhận và xác thực bằng đất sét trong Late Uruk, đặc biệt sự dịch chuyển toward việc đặt thông tin số trực tiếp trên bề mặt bền trong khi nhiều phương tiện cũ vẫn cùng tồn tại.

historical_change.from: Số lượng và sự xác thực được xử lý qua nhiều thiết bị và thực hành đất sét cùng tồn tại, gồm counters, envelopes, sealings và các bề mặt ghi số.
historical_change.to: Thực hành ghi nhận ngày càng đặt thông tin số trực tiếp trên bề mặt đất sét bền, đôi khi cùng dấu xác thực, trong khi các phương tiện cũ vẫn tiếp tục chồng lấn.

primitives.statement: Late-Uruk administrative recording and authentication used several clay-based practices and devices rather than one uniform recording medium.
primitives.time_scope: Late Uruk, especially the late fourth millennium BCE
primitives.place_scope: Southern Mesopotamia and associated Late-Uruk administrative contexts

primitives.statement: Numerical information was materialized through clay counting and recording practices, with the strongest continuity into proto-cuneiform lying in numerical systems rather than in a secure one-to-one inheritance of every sign form.
primitives.time_scope: Late prehistoric to Late Uruk transition, bounded to evidence relevant to early Mesopotamian recording
primitives.place_scope: Mesopotamian and related contexts represented in the approved research

primitives.statement: Some hollow clay envelopes enclosed counters, and some envelopes also carried exterior impressions or sealings that placed information or authentication on the outside surface.
primitives.place_scope: Late-Uruk administrative contexts represented in the approved source set

primitives.statement: Numerical tablets could carry quantity information directly as impressions on a durable clay surface, and sealing or authentication marks could coexist on such recording surfaces.
primitives.place_scope: Southern Mesopotamia and related Late-Uruk administrative sites represented in the approved source set

primitives.statement: Tokens, envelopes, sealings, numerical tablets and early written tablets belonged to overlapping recording and authentication practices; a simple token-to-tablet replacement genealogy is not established.
primitives.time_scope: Formation period around the late fourth millennium BCE
primitives.place_scope: Mesopotamian recording traditions covered by the approved research

primitives.statement: Growth in administrative and institutional scale coincided with strong demand for records and authentication, without establishing administration as the sole cause of writing or a one-way causal sequence.
primitives.place_scope: Urban and institutional contexts in southern Mesopotamia represented by the approved evidence

primitives.statement: Within Late-Uruk recording practice, numerical information increasingly appeared directly on durable clay surfaces, sometimes alongside authentication marks, while older and parallel clay practices continued to coexist.
primitives.time_scope: Late Uruk, late fourth millennium BCE
primitives.place_scope: Southern Mesopotamia and related Late-Uruk administrative contexts

primitives.statement: Early records support identification of accounting or administrative contexts more securely than fine distinctions among market exchange, tax, tribute, redistribution, labor obligation or ownership.
primitives.time_scope: Proto-cuneiform and immediately relevant formation contexts
primitives.place_scope: Early Mesopotamian administrative corpora represented in the approved sources

primitives.statement: A feedback relationship between expanding institutions and improved record systems is plausible: institutions could demand more records, and better records could increase institutional capacity.
primitives.place_scope: Institutional contexts represented in the approved evidence

limitations: Do not turn the parallel ecology into a single mandatory developmental sequence.
Do not present Neolithic tokens as a millennia-long standardized accounting code.
Do not claim continuity for individual non-numerical sign shapes without separate support.
The statement describes a class of practices, not a universal feature of every envelope.
It does not establish exterior impressions as a single transitional step toward tablets.
A numerical tablet does not by itself identify the commodity, transaction mechanism or named actor.
Do not describe this as wholesale replacement of envelopes or tokens.
Temporal overlap does not establish the exact contribution of each practice.
Do not narrate a deterministic evolutionary ladder.
Administration is a major formation pressure, not a monocausal explanation.
Co-occurrence does not prove which side caused the other.
The change is a shift in practice, not proof of a single invention event.
Increasing direct surface recording does not imply immediate or complete replacement of counters, envelopes or sealings.
Do not label a specific economic mechanism unless the evidence supports it.
This boundary need not be narrated unless the chosen telling approaches it.
This is a medium-confidence feedback model, not a completed causal verdict.
Do not back-project later institutional effects as established Late-Uruk facts.

writer_contract: Author from this bounded historical world and its historical change. Boundaries limit claims but are not lines that must be narrated. Use the evidence broker only to verify or sharpen a telling already chosen from this substrate; do not discover the story by surveying evidence records.
